text:
misha: heads-up — ran the nightly perf suite for hybrid quant (fp8+int8 path) on the 8k context test and saw TPS drop ~18% compared to last week. looks correlated with prefill windows; decode-only workloads are fine.
anya: can you paste the perf plot / raw numbers? which model and hardware?
misha: model=redwood-13b-hybrid, hw=a100-40, ctx=8192, microbatch=16. attached top-level numbers: 
```
prefill tps: 42 -> 34 (-19%)
decode tps: 98 -> 95 (-3%)
avg ttft(prefill start): 140ms -> 210ms
```
misha: CPU/GPU utilization looks normal but KV cache eviction spikes line up with the prefill stalls. trace shows frequent full-eviction cycles inside long prefill sequences.
perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/test/2026/1836789012 (shows kv_evictions/sec and per-kernel latency) :chart_with_upwards_trend: 
sam: my 2c — when quant path toggles from fp8 to int8 dequant on the hot path, we pay memcpy/dequant twice for prefill because of KV layout mismatch. could be causing TTFT regression for prefill-only workloads.
raj: can you share the kernel selection log? maybe the runtime is picking the slower fallback kernels for large sequence lengths.
misha: pasted snippet from logs:
```
[2026-03-12T05:10:12Z] kernel_selector: selected=matmul_fp8_fast for layer 0..10
[2026-03-12T05:10:13Z] kernel_selector: fallback=matmul_dequant_gemm for layer 11..40 (reason=kv_layout_mismatch)
[2026-03-12T05:10:13Z] kv_cache: eviction_start seq=4096 reason=buffer_pressure window_ms=25
```
anya: interesting — fallback is per-layer and coincides with mid-prefill. if fallback happens once per request it might be fine, but if it oscillates across layers that's bad.
sam: another experiment: try reducing microbatch from 16 -> 4 and lower batch_window_ms from 25 -> 10. that reduces concurrency and should avoid large KV eviction bursts. you'll trade TPS for more stable TTFT.
raj: also try turning on sticky-kv-layout: true (runtime flag) — forces single layout across quant modes, avoids dequant churn. config snippet: 
```
runtime.flags = {
  sticky_kv_layout: true,
  kv_eviction_threshold: 0.8,
  batch_window_ms: 12
}
```
misha: test run with sticky_kv_layout=true + microbatch=8 done: prefill TPS improved from 34 -> 37, TTFT reduced from 210ms -> 160ms, still not back to baseline.
perf-bot: perf diff: https://perf.redwood/diff/1836789012?cmp=last_week shows kernel-level breakdown: dequant memcpy accounted for ~12% of prefill latency increase, while eviction latency accounted for ~45%.
anya: eviction being dominant suggests we need to change scheduler heuristics: avoid large batch windows that cause many concurrent prefills to allocate competing KV buffers. can we implement a quick mitigation: cap total_prefill_inflight to 4 per-worker?
raj: +1. quick patch: add inflight_prefill_limit=4 and a soft backoff on prefill start that prefers continuing decode streams.
sam: we should also add a kernel-selection guard: if a fallback would cause dequant memcpy > 5ms for this sequence length, prefer alternative packing/tiling instead of per-layer fallback.
misha: ack. i'll run a 3-hour smoke with inflight_prefill_limit=4 & sticky_kv_layout + batch_window_ms=12. command i'm using: 
```
tools/bench/run_perf.sh --model redwood-13b-hybrid --ctx 8192 --quant hybrid --microbatch 8 --flags sticky_kv_layout=true,inflight_prefill_limit=4,batch_window_ms=12
```
anya: ping me when you have results, might be worth a canary roll to dedicated pool if it stabilizes.
perf-bot: created perf-issue #4578: "prefill KV eviction + quant fallback regression" and attached traces.
misha: thanks — opening an RFC for longer-term fix (kernel-selection heuristics + KV layout compatibility) and will paste link here. short term: canary with inflight_prefill_limit and sticky_kv_layout.
sam: fwiw we should add an automated microbenchmark that stresses long prefill paths under hybrid quant and alert if prefill TPS regresses >10% vs baseline.
anya: agreed. also add a synthetic test that toggles quant-mode mid-prefill to catch layout churn.
raj: i'll sketch a patch for the scheduler tomorrow.
misha: cool. i'll post results in this thread once the 3-hour run completes. :thumbsup:
